Step 1: Give Claude its two superpowers

This runs on two connectors inside Claude , and both take about a minute.

⚡ Get Higgsfield MCP, 100 free credits for new users

- Tap here to open Higgsfield MCP and copy your MCP link from that page.

- In Claude: Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector, paste the link. Higgsfield can now generate visuals directly inside your chats.

- In the same Connectors screen, enable the Indeed connector so Claude can read live job listings.

That is the entire setup. No code, no downloads.

Step 2: The list. Feed Claude your resume

Attach your actual resume, not a summary you typed from memory. Claude uses it twice: once to match your real experience against live listings, and again later to write your portfolio's about line. Paste this with the file attached.

Here's my resume. [attach your resume]

You are my job-hunting agent. Using the Indeed connector:

1. Read my resume so you know exactly what I do and my level.
2. Search Indeed for roles posted in the last two weeks that genuinely fit. Cast a wide net and score every listing out of 100.
3. Show me the top 25 as a clean table: Company, Role, Location, Match /100, and why I fit in one short line. Sorted by score, tight enough to read on a phone.
4. Under the table, tell me in three bullets what these companies keep asking for that my resume alone can't show.

Nothing generic.

What comes back

A scored table of the top matches, sorted, with a one-line reason you fit each. Then the part most people miss: three bullets on what these companies keep asking for that a resume can't show. Showreels, consistent branding, proof of finished work. That gap is exactly what the next prompt closes.

Step 3: The portfolio that builds itself

Now attach 5 to 10 of your best pieces. Photos, clips, designs, screenshots of finished work, whatever shows what you can do. Quality beats quantity, pick the ones you would show in an interview. Paste this in the same chat so Claude still has your resume and the list.

Now here's my work. [attach 5-10 photos or clips of your work]

You are my creative director and my agent. Using the list above:

1. Use Higgsfield MCP to turn my pieces into exactly what those companies keep asking for: a cinematic hero cover, branded versions of my best pieces, and a 20-30 second showreel with one consistent grade, led by the work that fits the top matches.
2. Build me a clean one-page portfolio from it that I can share as a single link: showreel up top, selected work, one line about me aimed at these roles, and a contact button. Dark, modern, expensive-looking. Give me the link on its own line.
3. For every match above 85, write a tailored three-sentence pitch that references their actual job description and the exact piece in my portfolio they should look at, with the link attached.
4. Then ask me one thing only: GO to submit the top matches one by one, or SEND ME so I can apply myself.

One-line progress updates. Don't ask me anything else. Make it look like I paid an agency.

Step 4: Review, then say GO

Claude shows you the portfolio link, then the tailored pitches, then stops. Nothing sends until you say so. Type GO and it starts submitting the top matches one by one with your portfolio link attached, or SEND ME if you want to fire them off yourself.

Open the portfolio link on your phone before you say GO. That link is the first impression every company gets, and if one piece feels weak, tell Claude to swap it in plain English.

Make it actually land

Three things separate the people who get replies from the people who blast and pray.

- Rerun prompt 1 every week. Listings turn over fast, and the two-week window keeps you in the fresh pile.

- Keep the pitches at three sentences. Recruiters skim. The portfolio link does the heavy lifting, the pitch just has to earn the click.

- Update the portfolio when your work improves. One strong new piece at the top changes how the whole page reads.

This whole flow is one loop: research, design, outreach. The same setup that used to take weeks of tabs now runs in one chat, and that is the actual unlock here.

New users get 100 free credits through this link , which is enough to build the portfolio assets and see the whole flow work. Past that it is a paid tool, the free credits are for trying it properly.

No. Setup is pasting one connector link into Claude 's settings and toggling Indeed on. After that it is two prompts and the word GO.

No. It researches, builds, and drafts everything, then stops and waits. Nothing is submitted until you type GO, and you can always pick SEND ME and apply yourself with the pitches it wrote.

If your work can be shown on a screen, yes. Photographers, editors, designers, 3D artists, social media managers, even developers with product screenshots. The portfolio adapts to whatever you feed it, the showreel just needs pieces worth showing.

Blasting one generic resume at 500 jobs is spam, and it is also what everyone else is doing. This is the opposite: every application is scored for real fit first, and every pitch references the actual job description and the exact piece of your work that proves it. Fewer, better, faster.

source_metadata.title: Make Your AirPods Sound 10x Better (The Settings Apple Buried)
source_metadata.access_status: Public page fetched successfully; visible article content available

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
Why your AirPods sound quiet out of the box

Two things are working against you from day one. First, iOS ships with a safety limiter that meters your headphone audio in decibels and quietly pulls loud playback down. Second, the tuning layer that makes AirPods actually shine is buried four menus deep in Accessibility, because Apple built it for hearing support and never advertised it as an audio upgrade.

Every setting below is free, built into iOS, and takes about 90 seconds total. Connect your AirPods first, none of these menus fully appear until they are in your ears.

Step 1: Turn on Headphone Accommodations

Settings > Accessibility > Audio & Visual > Headphone Accommodations . Flip it on.

What it actually does: this is a real-time tuning layer that re-shapes the sound on supported Apple and Beats headphones. It amplifies the soft details that normally get lost, background instruments, reverb tails, the quiet half of a mix, without just making everything louder. Think of it as a smart EQ plus a gentle compressor that Apple runs on-device.

It works with AirPods 2nd gen and later, all AirPods Pro, AirPods Max, wired EarPods, and most modern Beats. Third-party earbuds over plain Bluetooth do not get it.

Step 2: Balanced Tone, slider to Strong

Inside Headphone Accommodations, under Tune Audio For, you get three curves and three strengths. Here is what they mean so you are not guessing:

- Balanced Tone boosts soft sounds evenly across the whole frequency range. Music sounds fuller everywhere. This is the one you want.

- Vocal Range pushes the mids. Great for podcasts and calls, makes music sound thin.

- Brightness pushes the treble. Adds sparkle, gets fatiguing fast.

Then Slight, Moderate, Strong is just how hard the boost works. Strong is the maximum effect. Balanced Tone plus Strong is the combo that makes people go 🤯 the first time they A/B it. Use the Play Sample button and toggle it live, the difference is not subtle.

Step 3: Turn off Mono Audio

Same menu, Accessibility > Audio & Visual > Mono Audio . Make sure it is OFF.

What it actually does: Mono Audio folds the left and right channels into one identical signal in both ears. It exists for people who hear from one side, and it is a genuinely important accessibility feature. But if it got flipped on at some point, it is silently deleting your stereo image, the instrument separation, the width, the parts of a song that move between your ears. Off means full stereo.

Step 4: Turn on Music Haptics

Settings > Accessibility > Music Haptics . Flip it on (iOS 18 and later).

What it actually does: your iPhone's Taptic Engine plays synced vibrations that follow the track, so you literally feel the bassline through the phone in your hand or pocket. To be clear, the AirPods themselves do not vibrate, this is the phone. It works with Apple Music and a growing list of apps. Gimmick? A little. But holding your phone during a heavy drop hits different, and the battery cost is negligible.

Step 5: Kill the loudness warning

This is the one everyone actually came for. Two switches, same menu:

- Settings > Sounds & Haptics , scroll down, turn OFF Reduce Loud Sounds .

- Tap Headphone Safety , turn OFF Reduce Loud Audio .

What it actually does: iOS constantly measures your headphone output in decibels. With these on, it caps playback at a target level (somewhere between 75 and 100 dB) and after enough sustained loud listening it fires that notification and force-drops your volume mid-song. Turning both off removes the cap and stops iOS from touching your volume slider.

Two honest notes. In some regions, mostly the EU, the headphone notification is required by law and iOS will not let you fully disable it. And the warning exists for a real reason, sustained very loud sessions do permanent damage, so take the cap off because you want control, not because you want every session at maximum. Your ears are the one piece of hardware with no replacement part.

Bonus: three more that stack on top

The video covers the core six, but while you are in Settings these three stack with everything above:

- Late Night EQ : Settings > Apps > Music > EQ > Late Night . Compresses the dynamic range so quiet parts jump up. It is the oldest perceived-loudness trick on iPhone and it still works.

- Personalized Spatial Audio : Settings > [your AirPods] > Personalized Spatial Audio . Uses the Face ID camera to scan your ears and tailor the spatial mix to your actual head shape.

- Ear Tip Fit Test (AirPods Pro): same AirPods settings page. A bad seal leaks all your bass before it reaches your eardrum, this test catches it in 10 seconds.

And since you are already deep in Settings, check every secret phone code and run the 60-second check that nobody is inside your iPhone while you are there.

Frequently asked questions

AirPods 2nd generation and later, every AirPods Pro, AirPods Max, wired EarPods, and most modern Beats models. It is an Apple/Beats chip feature, so third-party earbuds over standard Bluetooth do not get it.

The limiter itself does not protect you, your listening habits do. Turning it off gives you back the volume slider, it does not make loud sessions safe. Sustained listening near max volume causes permanent hearing damage, so use the headroom for badly-mastered quiet tracks, not for living at 100%.

In some regions, mostly the EU, the loud-listening notification is legally required and iOS greys the toggle out or turns it back on. Reduce Loud Sounds and Reduce Loud Audio can still usually be disabled, which stops the mid-song volume drops.

No. AirPods pair to Android as plain Bluetooth earbuds, but Headphone Accommodations, Personalized Spatial Audio, and Music Haptics are all iOS-side features and stay behind on the iPhone.

It uses the Taptic Engine, so technically yes, but in normal listening the hit is negligible. If you are squeezing the last 2% before a charger, toggle it off.

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
What you're about to build

Claude just added a native Indeed connector, and it changes the job hunt completely. You connect the two once, hand Claude your resume, and it reads live Indeed listings, ranks the ones you're actually a strong fit for, and rewrites your resume for each one on the Harvard guide and the Google XYZ formula.

Here's the honest part the hype skips. The Indeed connector can find and read jobs, but it cannot click apply for you. The actual submitting is done by Claude for Chrome , the browser extension that drives Indeed the way you would, filling and sending each application.

So the real system is two tools working together. The connector is the brain that finds and tailors. Claude for Chrome is the hands that apply. Set both up once and the whole thing runs while you sleep.

Prefer ChatGPT? Here's the same play with ChatGPT Agent Mode . This is the Claude version, and the native connector makes the finding step far cleaner.

What you need first

Five minutes of setup and you're running:

- A paid Claude plan. Connectors and Claude for Chrome are on the paid tiers.

- An Indeed account with your profile filled in and your resume uploaded there.

- Your resume as a PDF on your computer, so you can drop it straight into Claude.

- The Claude for Chrome extension installed for the applying step. Add it to Chrome and sign in with the same Claude account.

Get those four ready and every step after this takes under a minute.

Step 1 - Connect Claude to Indeed

Open Claude . In the sidebar click Customize, then Connectors, then Browse connectors. In the search box type Indeed, and when it shows up under Anthropic and Partners, click the plus button to add it.

Claude hands you off to Indeed to authorize. You'll see the permissions it asks for, searching job listings and reading your Indeed profile, so it can match roles to you. Approve it and you land back in Claude, fully connected.

That's the entire connection. Claude can now pull live Indeed listings inside any chat.

Step 2 - Upload your resume and find your best-fit jobs

Start a new chat, drag your resume PDF into it, then paste the prompt below. This tells Claude to use the Indeed connector, pull everything posted recently, and rank it honestly instead of dumping every listing on you.

Claude comes back with a ranked shortlist, strong fits at the top, plus a straight read on where you're stretching. That shortlist is what everything else runs on.

Here's my resume (attached). Using the Indeed connector, find every job posted in the last 5 days that fits my experience. Rank them from strongest to weakest fit and give me an honest assessment: the roles I'm a top candidate for, the ones that are a stretch, and the exact keywords each posting's screening system is scanning for. Put it in a clean list with the company, title, location, salary, and link.

Step 3 - Rebuild and tailor on the Harvard guide + Google XYZ formula

A generic resume dies in the first ten seconds. Two frameworks fix that, and Claude applies both automatically.

The Harvard resume guide is the standard Harvard hands its own students: tight, action-led bullets, no fluff, quantified results. The Google XYZ formula is the pattern recruiters are trained to look for, Accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z . Every bullet becomes a result with a number on it.

Paste this and Claude rebuilds your resume into a master template, then spins a tailored version for each role on your shortlist, matching the language and keywords in each posting.

Rebuild my resume into a master template that follows the Harvard resume guide exactly, plus the Google XYZ formula (Accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z) on every bullet. Then create a tailored version for each of the top roles you just found, matching the exact keywords and language in each job description. Strip anything a hiring manager would flag in the first 10 seconds, and keep each one to a single page.

Step 4 - Apply for real with Claude for Chrome

This is the step the viral clips skip. The Indeed connector found and tailored everything, but it has no apply button. To actually submit, you hand off to Claude for Chrome .

Install the extension, open Indeed in Chrome, and make sure you're logged in. Open the Claude sidebar and give it your shortlist and the tailored resumes. It drives the page the way you would: opens a listing, fills the application, attaches the right resume version, and submits.

Start with Easy Apply listings. Those are the ones Claude can complete end to end without leaving Indeed. Paste this to kick it off.

I'm logged into Indeed in this tab. Here is my shortlist and the tailored resume for each role. Go through the list one by one, open each posting, and complete the application using the matching tailored resume. Start with the Easy Apply listings. If a posting asks something you can't answer from my resume, pause and ask me. Show me the first three before you submit them, then keep going.

Step 5 - Let it run while you sleep

Once you've watched the first few go out and you trust how it's filling things in, let it work the rest of the shortlist in batches. A few things keep it smooth and keep you in control:

- Prioritize Easy Apply. Applications that bounce you to an external company site are slower and more likely to stall, so let Claude clear all the Easy Apply ones first.

- Keep a tracking sheet. Ask Claude to log every job it applied to with the date and a link, so you never double apply and you know exactly where to follow up.

- Batch, don't blast. Real submissions take time and Indeed watches for spam, so steady batches beat trying to fire off a thousand in an hour. The number was never the point, not doing this by hand is.

- Refresh daily. Re-run Step 2 each morning for jobs posted in the last day, and Claude keeps feeding fresh roles into the machine.

That's the full loop. The connector finds and tailors, Claude for Chrome applies, and you review and sleep.

All the prompts, in order

Here's the full sequence in one place. Run them top to bottom, resume attached at the first one.

1) FIND AND RANK (attach your resume, in Claude):
Using the Indeed connector, find every job posted in the last 5 days that fits my resume, rank them strongest to weakest fit, and give an honest assessment plus the exact keywords each posting scans for. List company, title, location, salary, link.

2) REBUILD AND TAILOR (in Claude):
Rebuild my resume on the Harvard guide plus the Google XYZ formula, then make a tailored one-page version for each top role, matching each posting's keywords.

3) APPLY (in Claude for Chrome, logged into Indeed):
Go through my shortlist, open each posting, complete the application with the matching tailored resume, start with Easy Apply, ask me anything you can't answer, and show me the first three before submitting.

4) TRACK AND REPEAT (in Claude):
Log every application with date and link in a sheet, then each morning find new jobs posted in the last day and add them to the list.

One heads up before you let it loose

Claude for Chrome is acting on your behalf inside a real logged-in account, and it's new, so treat the first session like a test drive. Watch the first handful of applications the whole way through and confirm it's answering questions the way you actually would. Keep everything on your applications truthful, a tailored resume is still your resume. And you can disconnect the Indeed connector or pause the extension any time from settings.

What you're about to do

ChatGPT plays recruiter, rebuilds your resume to Harvard's standard using their actual guide, then turns on Agent Mode to find matching jobs and apply to them for you, tailoring each application. Download the Harvard guide first, then run the four prompts in order.

Download: the real Harvard resume guide

This is the guide Harvard hands its own students. Save it, then upload it into ChatGPT at Step 2 so it rebuilds your resume to that exact standard.

Step 1 — Find your best-fit roles

Upload your current resume into ChatGPT, then paste this:

Act as a senior recruiter. Based on my resume, list the 20 job titles I'm most qualified for and the exact keywords ATS systems scan for in each.

Step 2 — Rebuild it on the Harvard guide

Upload the Harvard guide you just downloaded, then paste this:

Here's the Harvard resume guide (attached). Rebuild my resume into a master template that follows this guide exactly, plus the Google XYZ formula, and strip every red flag a hiring manager spots in under 10 seconds.

Step 3 — Turn on Agent Mode and build your job list

Click the plus, then More, then Agent Mode. Then paste this:

Go to LinkedIn and Indeed, find every job matching these titles posted in the last 7 days, and build me a spreadsheet with the link, a match score, and a custom tailored version of my new resume for each one.

source_metadata.access_status: Public page fetched successfully; visible article content available

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
What you are actually using

The tool is winget , Microsoft's official package manager. It ships built into Windows 11 and modern Windows 10, so you are not installing anything sketchy, it is already on your machine.

One rule before we start: admin CMD executes anything you paste with full power. Only paste commands you understand or got from a source you trust. Everything below is explained line by line.

Step 1: See every app you have (and what is outdated)

Press Windows + R , type cmd , hit Enter. Then paste this:

winget list

Step 2: The basic upgrade command

You will see every application, the version you are on, and the upgrade available. This command upgrades all of them:

It works, but it is slow, and you have to sit there approving upgrades one by one. Here is the fix.

winget upgrade --all

Step 3: Full autopilot (the command from the video)

This time run CMD as admin: press your Windows key , type cmd , right click Command Prompt, Run as administrator . Then paste this one line:

It auto-accepts the license prompts and installs everything silently, one by one, while you go play video games or something 🤯

If a few apps show an unknown installed version and get skipped, run it again with --include-unknown added to the end.

winget upgrade --all --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements

Secret command 1: Unlock Ultimate Performance mode

Microsoft ships a hidden power plan called Ultimate Performance that removes the micro-throttling your PC does to save power. It is invisible until you run this in admin CMD:

Then press Windows + R , type powercfg.cpl , hit Enter, and select Ultimate Performance from the list. Honest note: the gains are real but biggest on desktops and plugged-in laptops. On battery it will drain you faster, that is the trade.

powercfg -duplicatescheme e9a42b02-d5df-448d-aa00-03f14749eb61

Secret command 2: God Mode

This creates a folder on your desktop containing every single Windows setting that exists, all 200+, in one flat list. No more digging through Settings menus:

md "%USERPROFILE%\Desktop\GodMode.{ED7BA470-8E54-465E-825C-99712043E01C}"

Secret command 3: Purge the junk your PC hoards

Windows quietly hoards gigabytes of temp files. This clears them instantly and safely, anything in use gets skipped automatically and Windows rebuilds what it actually needs:

Your PC is not the only device hiding settings from you. The AirPods settings Apple buried and the secret phone codes master list do the same job for the rest of your hardware.

del /q /f /s "%TEMP%\*"

Frequently asked questions

Yes. winget is Microsoft's official package manager, built into Windows. The packages come from Microsoft's curated repository, it is the same tech IT departments use.

Your Windows is missing the App Installer. Open the Microsoft Store, search for App Installer , update it, then reopen CMD. Windows 11 ships with it, older Windows 10 sometimes needs the update.

Mostly no. Steam, Epic and most launchers update their own games. winget handles your applications, browsers, editors, players, tools, which is where the outdated stuff actually piles up.

It removes power throttling, which kills the micro-stutters that feel like lag. On a desktop or plugged-in laptop the difference is noticeable in heavy games. It is not a magic 2x, anyone promising that is lying to you.

Yes. The %TEMP% folder is disposable by design, Windows recreates whatever it needs. Files currently in use are skipped automatically, so you cannot break a running app with it.

source_metadata.title: The Door to Anywhere: Walk Out of Your Room Into Any World
source_metadata.access_status: Public page fetched successfully; visible article content available

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
Step 1: Film the door

Set your phone or camera on a tripod facing a closed door and leave it completely still. No handheld, no repositioning, no drifting. A locked off camera is what makes the illusion work, because the moment the frame moves the two halves stop lining up.

Walk into frame, reach for the handle, and open the door. Three or four seconds is plenty. What you actually need is a clean moment where your hand is on the handle and the door has just started to move.

If a cat wanders into your shot, leave it in. The imperfections are what make people believe the first half is real.

Step 2: Grab your start frame

Scrub back through the clip and screenshot the exact moment the door begins to open. That still is the start frame, and it is doing a lot of work: it carries your face, your clothes, the room, the lighting and the door position into the generated half.

Pick a frame where your face is clearly visible and nothing is motion blurred. A blurry start frame produces a second half where you look like a slightly different person.

Step 3: Open Higgsfield inside ChatGPT

In ChatGPT , open the plugins menu and select Higgsfield. Everything happens in the chat from here, and the model you want is Seedance 2.5 .

⚡ Get the Higgsfield plugin for ChatGPT

Seedance 2.5 is the part that matters. It holds a real person's identity from a single still while building a completely different world around them, which is exactly what this effect needs.

Step 4: Paste the prompt

Upload your start frame, paste this, and send it. This version builds a Minecraft world on the other side of the door.

Use Seedance 2.5 in Higgsfield for this generation.

The first frame is exactly the attached photo, unchanged.

The person in the photo opens the door in front of them. Their face, hair, outfit, skin tone and body proportions stay exactly identical to the photo throughout, and the interior around them stays exactly as it appears in the photo. The camera is completely static and locked for the entire shot, no panning, no zooming, no camera shake, no movement of any kind.

As the door swings open, instead of revealing the interior background, the doorway opens directly onto a Minecraft world seen from human eye level: standing on a grass block at ground level, a vast survival world stretches ahead in bright midday. Everything is built from one meter cubes locked to a strict grid, grass blocks with green tops and brown dirt sides, stone, oak logs, cobblestone. Every surface uses low resolution 16x16 pixel textures with hard pixel edges, no smoothing, no anti-aliasing, no rounded corners, no bevels, no realistic material shading.

The world is spectacular. A deep ravine cuts across the middle distance with a waterfall of flowing water blocks pouring into it, and glowing orange lava spilling from an exposed cave mouth in the far wall. Beyond it, enormous floating islands hang in the sky with vines and thin waterfalls trailing off their undersides. Giant cubic oak and spruce trees rise from the valley floor, canopies made of blocky leaf clusters. On a plateau in the far distance sits a huge player built castle of stone brick and glass, torches glowing along its walls. Square white clouds sit high overhead in a flat blue sky with a square sun. Distant terrain fades into Minecraft's characteristic render distance fog.

As the door opens, flat daylight spills through the doorway. The person steps forward through the doorway onto the grass blocks and begins to run freely and naturally across the world toward the ravine, relaxed and joyful, natural human running motion, consistent body proportions and identity held from the photo.

The person stays completely photoreal. Real skin, real hair, real fabric, real human anatomy, exactly as in the attached photo. They are never stylized, never blocky, never pixelated. The contrast between the photoreal person and the fully blocky world is the point of the shot, and the boundary is a clean hard cut at the door frame with real interior on one side and Minecraft on the other.

The world is alive with motion authentic to the game: the square clouds drift slowly in one straight line at a constant speed, water and lava animate downward in looping texture frames, torch flames flicker with tiny floating embers, and sheep, cows and chickens wander through the grass with stiff blocky walk cycles. All motion is slow, steady and mechanical, exactly like the real game, nothing organic or wind driven.

Lighting is Minecraft's flat block lighting, each cube face evenly lit as a single tone, hard edged shadows aligned to the block grid, no soft falloff, no bloom, no ambient occlusion gradients, no lens flare. The person is lit to match that same flat daylight once through the doorway, with a hard edged shadow on the grass blocks beneath them, shadow direction consistent with the square sun.

No transition effects of any kind, no glowing edges, no flashes, no sparkles, no portal particles, no warping or morphing at the door frame. The world is rendered exactly like vanilla Minecraft gameplay footage, not a realistic or ray traced or cinematic reinterpretation of it. Static locked camera throughout.

Step 5: Stitch the halves together

You now have two clips: your real footage, and the generated continuation. Upload both to the same chat and paste this.

Here are two clips. The first is my original footage, the second is the generated continuation.

Stitch them into one seamless video. Cut the first clip at the exact frame the door starts to open and join the second clip there. Match the color and exposure across the join so the cut is invisible, keep the original audio from the first clip running underneath, and export it vertical 9:16 at the highest quality available.

Make it any world you want

The prompt is built so the world is swappable. Everything from the third paragraph onward describes Minecraft, so replace that block and keep the rest.

Some that work well: an underwater trench with whales drifting past, a neon Tokyo alley in the rain, the surface of Mars with the Earth low on the horizon, a medieval castle courtyard mid tournament, or a cloud city above a storm.

Two things to keep whatever world you pick. Keep the locked camera, because it's the anchor that sells the join. And keep the instruction that you stay photoreal, because the model will otherwise start restyling you to match the world as you cross the threshold, and the whole effect collapses the moment your face changes.

The things that break it

A moving camera in the original. Even slight handheld drift means the generated half cannot match, and the join reads as a cut instead of one continuous shot.

A motion blurred start frame. The model reads your face from that single still. Blur it and you get a stranger.

Asking for effects at the doorway. Glows, sparkles and portal shimmer sound good and look like AI. The prompt explicitly bans them so the boundary stays a clean hard edge, which is far more convincing.

Cutting at the wrong frame when stitching. Join at the exact frame the door starts moving. A few frames early or late and you get a visible jump in the door's position.

Frequently asked questions

No. A phone on a tripod or propped against something solid is fine. The only real requirement is that it does not move at all while you film.

Seedance 2.5, through the Higgsfield plugin in ChatGPT. Get the plugin here , then select Seedance 2.5 when you send the start frame and prompt.

Almost always a soft or motion blurred start frame. Pick a sharper frame where your face is clearly readable. Keeping the line about staying photoreal in the prompt also stops the model restyling you to match the world.

Yes, that is the point of the structure. Swap the paragraphs describing the world and leave the camera, identity and no-effects instructions exactly as they are.

Three or four seconds. You only need the approach and the moment the door starts to open, since everything after that is generated.

source_metadata.title: Give Your AI Access to Every Insider Trade (Including Congress)
source_metadata.access_status: Public page fetched successfully; visible article content available

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
What this actually does

Three things, all from public records:

- Corporate insiders (CEOs, CFOs, directors): the biggest buys, the cluster buys, and who's dumping, straight from their SEC filings.

- Members of Congress (Pelosi and the rest): their disclosed trades, by ticker and date.

- Optional and advanced: if you connect your brokerage, Claude can flag big moves and mirror them, but only with your approval, never on its own.

It's all public data anyone can look up. This is an educational way to read it faster. It is not financial advice, and copying anyone's trades is risky.

Step 1: Plug the insider feed into Claude (2 minutes, free)

This uses the free, open-source OpenInsider MCP , which reads SEC Form 4 corporate-insider filings. No API key, no paid account.

Claude Desktop: open your config (Settings, then Developer, then Edit Config), paste this in, and restart Claude.

Claude Code: one line instead, claude mcp add openinsider -- npx -y openinsider-mcp .

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openinsider": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "openinsider-mcp"] }
  }
}

Step 2: Ask it about corporate insiders

Now just talk to it. Start with these three.

Show me the biggest insider buys filed this week, ranked, and tell me who's buying (CEO, CFO, director, 10% owner), the ticker, the share count, and the exact price they paid.

Now show me every cluster buy, where 2 or more insiders at the same company bought recently. That's the strongest signal on the site.

Is anyone dumping [TICKER]? Pull the recent insider sells and tell me if insiders are net buying or net selling.

Step 3: Track Congress (Pelosi and friends)

The OpenInsider MCP is corporate insiders only. Congressional trades are disclosed separately under the STOCK Act, so for those you point Claude at Capitol Trades , the free public tracker (Claude reads it in your browser).

Go to Capitol Trades and pull [politician]'s latest disclosed trades. List the ticker, buy or sell, the date, and the amount range, newest first.

Step 4: Turn it into a daily radar

Have Claude watch all of it for you and brief you every morning, so you never miss a move.

Build a scheduled task that runs every morning: scan for new insider buys over $1M and any new cluster buys, plus the newest disclosed trades from the members of Congress on my list, and send me a short plain-English brief. Watchlist: [your tickers + politicians].

Step 5 (advanced): mirror it through your brokerage

This is the part from the end of the video, and it's the riskiest, so read the disclaimer below first. If you connect the Robinhood MCP , Claude can take the radar a step further: flag unusual insider or Congress activity and place the trade for you, but only after you approve each one. It never trades on its own.

Full brokerage setup here: Give Claude Full Access to Your Robinhood .

Read this before you copy anyone

This is public data and an educational demo, not financial advice. Insiders and members of Congress can be wrong, late, or trading for reasons that have nothing to do with you, and their filings are often days old by the time you see them. Copy-trading is risky and you can lose money. If you connect a brokerage, Claude only ever places a trade after you approve it, never automatically. content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
The prompt

Open ChatGPT , upload a clear, front-facing, well-lit selfie, then paste this exactly as written. Do not soften it. The "brutally honest but constructive" line is what stops ChatGPT from handing you a polite nothing-answer.

The free plan handles this fine, image upload is all you need.

Act as a brutally honest but constructive facial-aesthetics and "looksmaxxing" coach. Analyze the selfie I uploaded like an editorial beauty report. Cover: facial symmetry, bone structure / jawline, eye area, skin quality, and overall harmony. Give me:
1. An honest attractiveness score out of 10.
2. My top 3 strongest features.
3. My top 3 areas to improve.
4. A realistic step-by-step "looksmax" plan (grooming, skincare, hair, fitness, style, posture) to raise my score. Natural, non-surgical advice only.
Be specific, not generic.

The photo decides the accuracy

A clear, front-facing photo in good lighting gives the most accurate read.

Bad lighting reads as bad skin. A weird angle reads as asymmetry. A filter defeats the entire point.

Natural daylight, camera at eye level, neutral expression, no filter. Give the model a real input and you get a real report.

How to read your score

The score is a vibe check from one photo, not a clinical measurement. Run it twice and the number can move. Do not re-roll until it flatters you, that kills the value.

The real output is everything under the number: the three features to lean into, the three areas to work on, and the step-by-step plan. Screenshot the plan, pick the two easiest items, start there.

If ChatGPT hedges on giving an exact number, let it. The plan is the part you act on.

The 30-day re-check

One run is a snapshot. Progress is the comparison.

Work the plan for 30 days, take a fresh selfie in the same lighting, then open a new chat, upload it, and paste this with your old report at the bottom. Comparing two reports tells you what actually moved. Staring at one number tells you nothing.

Act as the same brutally honest looksmaxxing coach. I have uploaded a new selfie taken 30 days after my previous report, in similar lighting. My previous report is pasted below. Compare the new selfie against that report: what visibly improved, what did not, and which parts of the plan are working. Then give me my next 3 highest-impact steps and an updated honest score out of 10.

Previous report:
[paste your previous report here]

Your face is biometric data. Act like it.

You are uploading your face to an AI service, so make that a decision, not an accident.

Only upload your own photo. Never run someone else's face through this without their clear consent.

If you do not want your image used for model training, turn that off first: ChatGPT Settings, then Data Controls, then switch off "Improve the model for everyone." Or run the whole thing in a Temporary Chat, which is not used for training and never lands in your history. In a normal chat, delete the conversation afterward if you want it gone.

And keep the output in perspective. This is a grooming plan from a language model, not a verdict on you. Use what helps, ignore what does not.

Frequently asked questions

Upload a clear selfie and ChatGPT scores your symmetry, jawline, eye area and skin out of 10, then builds a step-by-step glow-up plan.

Honest but constructive. The score comes with your three weakest features and how to fix them.

Yes, natural and step-by-step, not surgery. Grooming, skin, and habits that actually move the number.

Why you start now, before launch

GTA 5 created thousands of faceless YouTube channels that did nothing but post clips and grew to millions of views. GTA 6 is going to be the biggest entertainment launch in history.

Here is the move almost no one acts on: you do not wait. You build the channel now, with GTA 6 gameplay, so you already have an audience and a posting rhythm on day one. Getting in early is the whole advantage.

Step 1: Connect Higgsfield to Claude

Higgsfield plugs into Claude as a custom connector, so Claude can cut video for you.

In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. Name it Higgs, or anything you like, and paste in the Higgsfield connector link below. That is a one time setup.

https://higgsfield.ai/mcp

Step 2: The clip cutting prompt

Grab GTA 6 gameplay on YouTube and copy its link. Then paste this into Claude. It tells Higgsfield exactly how to cut the clips.

Using Higgsfield, take this GTA 6 gameplay: [paste the YouTube link]. Cut it into 5 vertical 9:16 clips, 20 to 30 seconds each. Pick the most cinematic and hype moments, add bold auto captions, and export them ready to post as YouTube Shorts.

Step 3: Make it original with your voice

Pure reuploads get demonetized, so you add yourself on top. Write a quick take or reaction and turn it into a voiceover with ElevenLabs , then lay it over the clip. Your voice and your angle are what make the clip original and keep it monetizable.

Step 4: Post daily and get in early

Batch a week of clips in one sitting, then post one a day. Shorts grow a channel fast but pay less than the hype, so use them to build the audience, then funnel people to longer videos and your other links.

Do this now and by the time GTA 6 actually launches you are not starting from zero. You already have the channel, the audience, and the workflow.

No, and that is the whole point. You build the channel now and get the audience and the posting habit locked in before launch day. Early movers win.

No. This is a faceless channel. You only need the gameplay footage, Claude plus Higgsfield to cut the clips, and a voiceover.

Claude is free to use, and both Higgsfield and ElevenLabs have free tiers to start. You can test the whole workflow without paying.

Use gameplay footage and add your own voice and commentary so the clip is transformative, not a pure reupload. Reuploads with nothing added get demonetized, your take is what keeps it safe and original.

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
Why these actually print money

Street interview pages like Street Poller (330K+ followers) rack up millions of views, but the views are not the money. The money is the placements. Brands pay to get their shirt worn on camera, their product named by a 'random' person, or a specific creator featured as the expert who just happens to have the perfect answer. It is native advertising dressed up as a vox pop.

Until now you needed a mic, a camera, a busy street, and a day of filming. You do not anymore. You can generate the exact same format on demand, for any brand, from your couch.

Step 1: Connect Higgsfield to Claude (one time, under a minute)

You only do this once. It connects Higgsfield to Claude so Claude can generate the videos for you.

- Open Higgsfield here and sign in. This is the MCP that powers the whole thing.

- Copy the MCP connection URL it shows you.

- In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, and click Add custom connector. Paste that URL and name it Higgsfield.

- At the very top of the chat, switch your model to Fable 5. That is the brain doing the heavy lifting.

Step 2: The prompt (start here)

This is the whole trick. Paste this into Claude on Fable 5, swap the two brackets, and let it run. Simplicity wins here, one clean question plus one planted answer is all it takes.

Using the Higgsfield MCP, make me a street interview.

An attractive female host holding a microphone stops 4 random people on a busy city street and asks them: "[YOUR QUESTION HERE]"

Make each person a completely different look, age, and vibe. Keep every answer short, casual, and real. The last person casually says: "[THE PRODUCT OR PERSON YOU ARE PROMOTING], [one line on why it is great]."

Shoot it vertical 9:16, handheld, candid UGC style, real street background with ambient noise. Give me each answer as its own clip so I can stitch them together.

Step 3: The comprehensive prompt (for a sharper result)

Once the basic one is working, use this longer version when you want real control over the host, the cast, and the candid look. It is built around an attractive female host so the clip holds attention.

Using the Higgsfield MCP, generate a viral man-on-the-street interview as a set of vertical 9:16 clips I can edit together.

THE HOST (the same woman in every clip):
An attractive woman in her mid 20s, styled and camera ready, holding a handheld microphone with a small blank mic flag. Warm, confident, playful energy. Busy city sidewalk in daytime, real pedestrians and street noise behind her.

THE LOOK:
Handheld camera, natural daylight, a slight push in on the punchy reactions, candid and slightly imperfect framing so it reads as real footage, not an ad.

THE QUESTION she asks every person:
"[YOUR QUESTION HERE]"

THE CAST (4 people, each a totally different look, age, ethnicity, and personality):
1. A confident young guy, quick and funny.
2. A stylish woman, a little sassy.
3. An older man, dry and matter of fact.
4. The plant: a relaxed, likeable person who casually answers "[PRODUCT OR PERSON YOU ARE PROMOTING], [one natural line on why it is great]" like it is obvious.

RULES:
Every answer is one or two short lines, spoken naturally, never a scripted ad tone. Build from mundane answers to the standout final one. Clear dialogue over ambient street audio.

OUTPUT:
One 3 to 5 second vertical clip per person (the host question plus their answer), plus one short clip of the host intro line. Delivered in order so I can stitch them straight together.

Step 4: Stitch it together

Higgsfield returns each person as its own vertical clip. Drop them into CapCut or any editor, back to back, mundane answers first and the standout answer last. Add auto captions, keep the cuts fast, and post. It looks like real street footage.

Step 5: Now get paid for it

This is where it turns into income. Every local business and creator wants viral style ads and has no idea how these are made.

- Generate one great sample for a niche (a restaurant, a gym, a product, a creator).

- DM local businesses and brands with that sample.

- Charge per video or per batch. You deliver same day, because it is one prompt.

Here is a DM that works:

Hey [name], love what you are building. I make viral street interview style ads, the kind that pull millions of views, fully custom for your brand. I can have one done for you this week. Want me to send you a sample?

Frequently asked questions

No. Claude Fable 5 writes the interview and Higgsfield generates every person, the host, and the street. You never leave your couch.

Higgsfield runs on credits and Claude needs Fable 5 access. A single interview costs very little in credits, and one paid client covers months of it.

Yes. Swap the question and the final planted answer to whatever you are selling, a brand, an app, a creator, a local shop. The format works for anything.

The candid handheld look reads as real footage. Keep it honest with your audience where it matters, and lean into the obvious-AI angle when you want it purely as entertainment.

Creators charge hundreds to a few thousand per street interview ad. Because you generate it in one prompt, almost all of that is margin.

Timing note: Higgsfield is running a one day window, July 23 from 6AM Pacific , where starting a trial or subscription unlocks a full week of unlimited generations on the platform, no credits counted on any model. Every prompt below becomes free to batch during that week.

⚡ Start the unlimited week here

The headshot generator (one selfie in, four pro headshots out)

The one from the video, I personally ran hundreds of these during the free window. One decent selfie replaces the photographer: run it on Nano Banana Pro (or GPT Image 2) with your photo attached as the reference, and swap any of the four looks for whatever your profile needs. Vault exclusive, this one is not in any other guide.

My attached photo is the identity reference. Generate 4 professional headshots of the person in the reference photo, preserving their exact likeness, facial features, skin tone, and hairstyle. One look per image: 1) CORPORATE: charcoal suit, crisp white shirt, soft light-gray studio backdrop. 2) STARTUP: plain black tee, moody dark backdrop, soft teal rim light. 3) CREATIVE: smart casual layers, warm tones, blurred golden-hour city background. 4) EDITORIAL: black and white, high contrast, dramatic side light. Every image: 85mm portrait lens look, f2.8 shallow depth of field, tack-sharp focus on the eyes, natural skin texture with pores (no plastic AI smoothing), relaxed confident expression with a slight natural smile, head-and-shoulders framing with a little headroom, 4:5 portrait crop, high resolution. No text, no watermarks, no logos, no accessories that are not in the reference photo.

The dating profile upgrade (the photos your profile is missing)

The photo half of the dating profile play. Run the dating profile prompt first, ChatGPT rates your profile, rewrites the bio, and tells you exactly which photos are weak and what kind of shot you are missing. Then this prompt generates those missing shots, run it on Nano Banana Pro (or GPT Image 2) with your best selfie attached as the identity reference, and swap the hobby slot for your real one. Vault exclusive, this prompt is not in the dating guide. Same rule as the headshots above, it preserves your exact likeness, so the result is your face on a better day, not a different person. Keep it honest, and retake the real shot when you can.

My attached photo is the identity reference. Generate 6 dating profile photos of the person in the reference photo, preserving their exact likeness, facial features, skin tone, body type, and hairstyle. One look per image: 1) GOLDEN HOUR CANDID: sitting at an outdoor cafe table at golden hour, laughing at something off camera, warm natural light. 2) HOBBY: [swap this slot for your real hobby: cooking in a bright kitchen, at the climbing gym mid-route, playing guitar on a couch], caught mid-action, genuinely focused. 3) DOG SHOT: crouched in a park next to a friendly golden retriever, one hand on the dog, big natural smile. 4) TRAVEL: standing at a scenic coastal overlook at dusk, relaxed posture, light jacket, hair slightly wind-blown, wider framing so the landscape shows. 5) NIGHT OUT: smart casual outfit, warm string lights and soft bokeh behind, relaxed confident half-smile toward camera. 6) FULL BODY: mid-stride walking toward camera on a tree-lined street, full outfit visible, natural gait. Every image: shot-on-a-phone realism, natural skin texture with pores (no plastic AI smoothing), slightly imperfect candid framing like a friend took it, consistent identity across all six, 4:5 portrait crop, high resolution. No text, no watermarks, no logos, no accessories that are not in the reference photo.

Why this prints right now

Faceless sports edit pages are exploding during the World Cup. Millions of views on edits the creator never filmed, just match highlights run through AI. Those views turn into creator payouts, brand shoutouts, and affiliate money.

And the second the World Cup ends you swap in the NFL playoffs, the NBA finals, UFC, whatever is in season, so the page never runs dry. The window is now, ride the wave while attention is peaking.

Step 1: Connect Higgsfield to Claude

Higgsfield plugs into Claude as a custom connector so Claude can pull and clip video for you.

In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. Name it Higgs, and paste in the link below. One time setup.

https://higgsfield.ai/mcp

Step 2: Grab the footage

Go to YouTube and search FIFA World Cup goal highlights (or your sport plus highlights). Open a clean highlight video and copy the URL.

Tip: the official and biggest highlight channels have the crispest footage, which makes a noticeable difference in the final edit.

Step 3: Run the edit prompt in Claude

Paste this into Claude along with the highlight URL. It pulls the footage through Higgsfield and cuts it into vertical shorts ready to style.

Using Higgsfield, take this [SPORT] highlight: [paste the YouTube link]. Cut it into vertical 9:16 clips, 15 to 20 seconds each, focused on the biggest moments, the goals and the skills. Export them ready to post.

Step 4: The funk finish (the part that makes it hit)

This is the step most pages will not tell you about. Drop the clip into CapCut , add a trending Brazilian funk or phonk track, and snap the hardest cut to the beat drop. Then add a slow-motion ramp on the goal, a glow on the player, and bold text with their name.

Always use the sound that is actually trending, not a random one, because the trending audio is what the algorithm pushes into more feeds. CapCut does all of this for free.

Step 5: Post daily and ride the wave

Batch a week of edits in one sitting, then post one or two a day. The moments that hit hardest: goals, last-minute winners, skill moves, and celebrations.

During a live tournament, post within hours of the match while the moment is still fresh. Consistency plus timing is the whole game.

How to actually make money from it

Once a page is pulling views, the money comes from a few places at once: the platform creator funds pay per view, brands pay for shoutouts and promo slots, you can affiliate sports products or fantasy apps, and eventually sell your own merch.

Because it is faceless, you can run more than one page in different sports and stack them.

Bonus: the any-sport swap

The workflow never dies, you just swap the sport and the money moment:

- World Cup -> the goal

- NFL playoffs -> the touchdown

- NBA finals -> the dunk or the buzzer beater

- UFC -> the knockout

- F1 -> the overtake

Whatever is in season, your page rides it.

Bonus: 3 edit styles so your page never looks repetitive

Rotate these in CapCut so every post feels fresh:

- Hard phonk: dark grade, heavy contrast, fast zoom-punches on the beat, glitch text. The classic edit look.

- Cinematic: slow ramps, warm grade, light leaks and lens flares, slower cuts. Feels premium.

- Retro VHS: grain, scanlines, 90s color, chunky text. Nostalgic and it stands out in the feed.

Bonus: your first 10 posts plan

Day 1, pick your sport and make the page with a clean name and a sharp logo. Days 1 to 3, batch 10 edits of the biggest current moments. Then post 1 to 2 a day, every day, for two weeks straight.

Reply to every comment in the first hour, that early engagement is what makes the algorithm push you. By the time the tournament peaks, your page is already rolling.

Claude and CapCut are free, and Higgsfield has a free tier to start. You can test the whole thing without paying.

Sports edit pages can blow up in days during a live tournament because demand is massive and good edits are thin on supply. Timing and consistency matter more than your follower count.

This is honest, no fake "it submitted everything for you" beat. Using the Claude in Chrome tool, Claude opens missingmoney.com in your own browser, searches every state's unclaimed-property database for you and your whole family, and builds a spreadsheet of every dollar you're owed.

Step 2: Let Claude pre-fill every claim

Once the spreadsheet looks right, paste this. Claude opens a tab for each claim and fills in everything that isn't your private info, then stops and tells you exactly what's left for you to enter.

Now open a new tab for each claim and fill in every field you can, everything except my personal identifying information. When you're done, stop and report back the exact list of fields I need to provide manually to submit each claim.

Step 1: Perplexity, build the fact bank

One prompt, 100 facts, a month of content sitting in a doc before you make a single video. You want weird and specific, not 'dogs have wet noses.' And the citations are not optional. Pet people fact-check you in the comments, and one wrong fact in a niche this passionate burns the exact trust you are about to charge $25 a month for.

Give me 100 lesser-known, weirdly specific facts about dog breeds, cite sources

Step 2: ChatGPT, turn each fact into a 25-second script

Paste one fact at a time after this prompt. The two constraints are the whole game. Hook in the first 3 words, because that is all the patience TikTok gives you. End on a cliffhanger, because the open loop drives the rewatch and the follow. And 25 seconds keeps completion rate high, because completion rate is what the algorithm pays for.

Turn this fact into a 25-second TikTok script. Hook in first 3 words. End on cliffhanger.

Step 3: ChatGPT image, lock one art style forever

Swap [breed] for whichever breed the fact covers and generate the visual. The rule that matters: reuse this exact phrasing every single time. The same pastel watercolor dog on every post makes the feed read as a brand instead of a random clip dump, and the brand look is what turns one viral video into a wave of follows.

Cute illustrated [breed], soft pastel watercolor style, white background

Step 4: CapCut, assemble and post 3 a day

CapCut does the production for free: auto-captions plus the built-in AI voiceover reading your script, so you never record a word. Illustration on screen, captions on, export. Post 3 a day to TikTok and cross-post the same files to IG Reels, a second algorithm for zero extra work. This step is where the playbook lives or dies. It works at 3 a day. It does not work at 3 a week.

1. New CapCut project, drop in the illustration
2. Paste the script as text, apply the free AI voiceover
3. Auto-captions on
4. Export
5. Post to TikTok, cross-post the same file to IG Reels
6. Repeat 3 times a day, every day

Step 5: Skool, the $25 a month community

Skool is free to start. Name the community 'Dog Training Cheat Sheets', price it at $25 a month, put the link in your bio. The weekly deliverable is one PDF cheat sheet built in Canva. Not a course, not coaching, one genuinely useful PDF a week. Roughly an hour of work for the asset people actually pay for, while the videos do the selling.

Name: Dog Training Cheat Sheets
Price: $25 a month
Deliverable: one Canva PDF cheat sheet per week
Placement: link in TikTok and IG bio

The math, and the honest part

480 members at $25 is $12,000 a month. That number is the goal, not week one, and the bridge between the two is volume. 3 posts a day is roughly 90 swings a month, and in pet niches one runner can fill a community overnight. Costs stay near zero: the captions and voiceover are free, the prompts run on free tiers, and Skool's free trial covers your launch. Once its monthly fee kicks in, your first handful of members covers it and everything after them is margin. The only real input is the streak. Most people quit at week two. content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
What this actually does

Most privacy guides hand you a list of 50 opt-out forms and wish you luck. This is different.

Claude does the work. It audits everything the internet has on you, writes every removal request, then uses your own browser to go site by site and submit each opt-out. When it figures out the pattern, it builds a scheduled task that re-runs every two weeks, catches anything that reappears, and removes you again. You set it up once.

First, turn on Claude in Chrome

Claude needs to use your browser to submit the opt-outs for you. Turn that on once.

In Claude, go to Settings, then Connectors , and enable Claude in Chrome (the "Use in Chrome" toggle). That is what lets Claude open each data-broker site and fill out the removal form on your behalf. Everything below runs in a single chat.

Step 1: Find everything the internet has on you

Start here. This pulls up every data broker and people-search site exposing you, with the exact opt-out link for each. Fair warning, the list is longer and more personal than you think.

Act as a privacy and data-removal expert. Search the web for everything publicly available about me and map my full exposure.

My details:
- Full name: [your full name]
- Current city and state: [city, state]
- Past cities, last 10 years: [list]
- Emails: [your emails]
- Phones: [your numbers]

List every data broker and people-search site exposing my information (name, current and past addresses, phone, email, age, relatives). Give it to me as a table I can track, with these columns:
1. Site name
2. The exact URL of my profile or listing (find it if you can)
3. The exact opt-out or "do not sell my info" link
4. What that site needs to remove me (email confirmation, CAPTCHA, ID, etc.)

Cover the big ones at minimum: Whitepages, Spokeo, TruePeopleSearch, Radaris, MyLife, Intelius, BeenVerified, PeopleFinders, FastPeopleSearch, and anything else you find on me.

Step 2: Write every removal request (and clean up Google)

Now Claude writes the exact opt-out request for each site, filled in with your details, and walks you through removing yourself from Google results too.

For every site on that list, write the exact opt-out or removal request I should submit, filled in with my details, and tell me precisely which fields to enter on each form.

Then show me, step by step, how to remove my personal information from Google Search using Google's "Results about you" tool and its personal-information removal form, including exactly what to paste and where.

Step 3: Let Claude submit them all

This is where Claude in Chrome earns its keep. It goes site by site, opens each opt-out page, fills in your request, and submits it. When a site throws a CAPTCHA or needs a code from your email, Claude pauses, tells you exactly what to do, then keeps going.

Using Claude in Chrome, go to every site on the list one by one. On each, open the opt-out page, fill in my removal request with my details, and submit it.

Follow these rules:
- Keep a live status table: site, action taken, result (Submitted / Pending confirmation / Needs me / Blocked).
- When a site shows a CAPTCHA, or asks for anything that personally identifies me (an ID upload, a code sent to my email or phone), stop, tell me exactly what to do, wait for me, then continue.
- If a removal needs email confirmation, tell me which inbox to check and what to click.
- Never give a site more information about me than it already has.

Work through the entire list and report the final status of each site.

Step 4: Put it on autopilot

Removing yourself once is not enough. Brokers re-scrape, and your data creeps back. This last prompt makes Claude schedule the whole process to re-run every two weeks, catch anything that reappeared, and remove you again, automatically.

Now create a scheduled task that runs this entire process automatically every two weeks:
- Re-scan every data broker and people-search site for my information.
- Compare against what you already removed and flag anything that has reappeared.
- Re-submit the opt-out for every site where I show up again.
- Send me a short summary each run: what came back, what you re-submitted, and what still needs me.

Keep it running until I am completely gone, and keep running it after that to keep me gone.

Tips for a clean wipe

- Check your email while it runs. A lot of brokers send a confirmation link you have to click.

- When Claude pauses for a CAPTCHA, solve it and tell it to continue.

- Search your own name in an incognito window before and after, so you can watch it working.

- Never pay a "removal service". This is your data and every opt-out is free.

- Only ever do this for yourself. Removing someone else's data without permission is a different thing entirely.

Why your data is even out there

Data brokers scrape public records, social media, and purchase histories, then sell a profile of you to anyone who pays: marketers, scammers, stalkers. Opting out is your legal right under "do not sell my info" rules. You are not hiding, you are taking back data that was harvested without you.

Frequently asked questions

Yes. Every data-broker opt-out is free, and you should never pay a removal service. All you need is Claude with Claude in Chrome turned on.

It is the connector that lets Claude use your browser. In Claude, go to Settings, then Connectors, and enable Claude in Chrome (the "Use in Chrome" toggle). Then Claude can open each site and submit the opt-out for you.

Completely. "Do not sell my info" and opt-out rights are yours by law. This only ever removes your own data, never use it on anyone else.

Brokers re-scrape over time, which is why the last prompt schedules Claude to re-check and re-remove you every two weeks automatically. That is what keeps you gone.

Mostly no. Claude submits everything itself and only pauses when a site needs a CAPTCHA or an email confirmation, then it tells you exactly what to do and continues.

The offer: $400 a month, flat

Dentists obsess over their Google rating because it is where new patients decide, and replying to reviews is the chore every office avoids. The negative ones scare them most. Dental practices have paid five-figure federal HIPAA penalties for the way they replied to a single review, and every practice manager has heard a story like it. So most offices freeze and reply to nothing while the one stars sit at the top of the profile doing damage.

You sell the disappearance of the problem. $400 a month, flat: we manage every Google review reply and run a review-request campaign monthly. That is the whole offer, no deck. The message below is the version you actually send, and you send it to the practice manager, because the headache is theirs.

Quick question: who replies to your Google reviews right now?

Most offices skip them because one wrong sentence in a reply can be a HIPAA problem, so the bad ones just sit there scaring off new patients.

I run a flat $400/month service for dental offices: every review answered in the doctor's voice with HIPAA-safe wording, plus a monthly review-request campaign so fresh 5-stars keep coming in.

Want me to draft replies to your 5 most recent reviews for free, so you can judge the quality before paying anything?

Step 1: Get access (Google Business Profile)

Get added as a Manager on their Google Business Profile. Free, about two minutes on their end, and you never touch a password. Manager access is enough to reply to reviews, which is all you need.

Do not make the office figure out Google's menus. Send them the exact instructions below, so onboarding becomes one invite click and the close feels effortless.

Send this to the office:

While signed into the Google account that runs your profile, search your practice name on Google. On your Business Profile, click the three-dot menu, then Business Profile settings, then People and access, then Add. Enter [your email] and set the role to Manager.

No passwords change hands, and you can remove me anytime.

Step 2: Route every new review to your inbox (Zapier)

Zapier's free tier covers one practice, with one catch nobody mentions: free zaps are single-step, one trigger and one action. So you build two tiny zaps instead of one fancy one.

Zap one emails you the moment a review lands. Zap two logs it to a Google Sheet, which quietly becomes your proof-of-work file for the monthly 'what am I paying for' conversation. A dental office gets maybe 10 to 30 reviews a month, so each review burns two of your 100 free tasks and you still have room to spare. Upgrade only when clinic three or four forces the task count up.

Zap 1. Trigger: Google Business Profile, New Review. Action: Email by Zapier, send the reviewer name, star rating, and review text to your inbox.

Zap 2. Trigger: Google Business Profile, New Review. Action: Google Sheets, Create Spreadsheet Row. Columns: Date, Clinic, Stars, Review, Reply posted (Y/N).

Step 3: Draft the reply (Claude)

Open Claude , paste the template below, drop in the review. Warm and human for the five stars, careful and short for the one stars.

The HIPAA rule inside the prompt does the heavy lifting. The reply never confirms anyone is a patient, not even inside a thank-you, and negative reviews get acknowledged and moved to a private phone call instead of debated in public. That single constraint is why a medical practice trusts you with this. Never edit it out.

You are replying to Google reviews as [Dr. Name], a [specialty] in [city].

Write a reply in 2-3 warm, human sentences.

Hard rules:
- Never confirm or imply the reviewer is a patient (HIPAA). No treatment details, no visit details, no dates.
- 4-5 stars: thank them and reflect one specific detail from their review.
- 1-3 stars: stay calm, never argue or explain, acknowledge the frustration and invite them to call the office to resolve it privately.
- No corporate filler like 'we strive for excellence'.
- Vary your openings so the replies never look templated.

Review: [paste review]

Step 4: Post it yourself (Google Business Profile)

Paste the approved replies into Google Business Profile manually. Two short sessions a week, 10 to 15 minutes per clinic, covers the volume a dental office actually gets.

Manual posting is the feature, not the bottleneck. A human reads every word before it goes live and nothing auto-posts, ever. When the doctor asks how you keep the AI from saying something stupid, the answer below is the one you give, word for word.

Nothing posts automatically. AI drafts every reply in your voice, then I personally read and approve each one before it touches your profile. If a reply ever feels off to you, it changes the same day.

Step 5: The monthly review ask (ChatGPT)

Once a month, run the campaign that keeps fresh five stars flowing. ChatGPT writes a one-line text, and the office sends it to their patient list through the patient texting tool they already use.

Keep it defensive on purpose. The patient list never leaves their systems and you only supply the message, so you hold zero patient data. That is exactly how this answer should sound when a practice manager asks. One rule: ask for honest reviews and never offer a discount or freebie in exchange, because Google removes incentivized reviews and the practice eats the risk.

ChatGPT prompt: Write 5 variations of a friendly one-sentence text from a dental office asking a patient to leave a quick Google review. Under 160 characters, no emojis, no pressure, include a [link] placeholder.

The one that works: Hey [name], if you have 30 seconds, it would mean a lot if you left us a quick Google review: [link]

The math: 10 clinics = $4K MRR

10 clinics x $400 = $4K MRR. Per clinic, the real workload is about 20 minutes a week of drafting and posting plus a 10-minute monthly campaign, so ten clinics lands around four hours a week.

The renewal logic is simple. Every review gets answered, the monthly ask keeps new five stars coming, the rating climbs, and new-patient calls climb with it. Nobody cancels a service they can watch working in their own search results. Land clinic one, screenshot the rating and review count on day one and day 60, and the next nine close off that screenshot.

Frequently asked questions

One careless reply to a bad review is a HIPAA problem, so most answer nothing. You take it off their plate.

Claude drafts every reply in the doctor's voice, HIPAA-safe. You review and post.

About four hours a week for ten clinics at $400 each, which is the $4K MRR.

Writing: Claude's lane, with one exception

Emails: Claude with memory. Memory is the whole difference. It carries your context, your projects, and your phrasing across conversations, so replies come out in your voice instead of assistant voice.

Human writing: Claude. Anything a real human will actually read. Captions, scripts, posts, pages. It is the model least likely to hand you something that smells like AI.

Brainstorming: ChatGPT . The one writing job I send elsewhere. ChatGPT gives you volume fast, 30 angles in seconds. Twenty-eight are throwaways. The two that are not pay for the whole exercise.

Research: four tools, four different jobs

Presentation research: Perplexity . Cited answers. You can check every claim before it goes on a slide, which matters when someone in the room will fact-check you live.

Deep research: Perplexity Comet . When one search is not enough. Comet works through sources on its own instead of leaving you with 40 open tabs and a headache.

Validating research: Gemini . Never let one model grade its own homework. Anything important gets run through Gemini as a second opinion before I act on it.

Trends: Grok . It is wired into X, so it catches what is blowing up right now while other models are still answering from last year.

Building: Claude Code, twice

Coding with no experience: Claude Code . You describe what you want in plain English. It writes the code, runs it, hits errors, and fixes them itself. That loop is the whole point. It handles the exact parts you would have needed the experience for.

Apps and skills: Claude Code. Same tool, bigger jobs. Full apps, automations, reusable skills you can run again next week. Once you start building instead of chatting, you do not go back.

Podcasts: NotebookLM . Drop in your notes, PDFs, and links, and it generates a two-host audio show about your material. I use it to turn dense research into something I can absorb on a walk. Free, and better than it has any right to be.

Images and video: where it gets crowded

Images: ChatGPT Image. Best at doing what you actually asked. Exact text in the image, specific layouts, edits stacked on top of edits without the whole picture melting.

Video: Google Omni. My current pick for raw text-to-video quality, and you edit by talking to it instead of re-rolling the whole clip. This space flips every few months. This is where it stands today.

content_payload.full_walkthrough_raw:
Step 1: Add the Meta Ads connector to Claude

This is the part that sounds hard and takes about thirty seconds.

- Search Google for facebook ads mcp and open the first result.

- Scroll to the bottom of that page and copy the connector URL.

- In Claude , open Settings , then Connectors , then Add custom connector .

- Name it Meta Ads and paste the URL in.

That is it. Claude can now read your ad account. Nothing has been given permission to spend anything yet, it is read and write access to campaign objects, which is why step 5 matters.

Step 2: Turn on the Higgsfield connector

The Meta connector gives Claude the data. The Higgsfield connector gives it the ability to actually make the video, and there is a free unlimited window open on it right now.

⚡ Open Higgsfield and claim the free unlimited window

- Tap here to open Higgsfield and activate the free window.

- Copy the MCP URL from that page.

- Add it in Claude the same way you added the Meta one, and name it Higgsfield .

Once redeemed you get 24 hours, so do the setup first and start generating second. Do not burn the window figuring out where the buttons are.

Step 3: Ask Claude what is already working

Do not skip to generating. The reason this beats making ads from scratch is that Claude can see your real numbers first, so the creative it builds is aimed at what already performs in your account instead of generic best practice.

Send this one first.

Use the data from my Meta Ads account to work out what is actually working
right now in my niche.

Pull my existing campaigns, ad sets and creatives, then tell me:
- Which of my ads have the best hook rate and hold attention longest.
- What those winners have in common: format, pacing, first frame, length,
  colour, on-screen text, offer framing.
- Which audiences and placements those winners performed best in.
- What is currently underperforming and why you think it is.

Then give me a short list of the viral creative angles I should test next,
ranked by how likely they are to beat my current best ad. Base it on my real
numbers, not general best practice. Be blunt about what is not working.

Step 4: Generate the ads and publish them

Now the second prompt. Claude uses Higgsfield to build the creative and the Meta connector to put it live, in the same conversation.

Note the last line. It creates the campaign paused on purpose.

Now use the Higgsfield MCP to create 10 viral ad variations based on the
winning angles you just found.

For each one:
- Build it around a single clear hook that lands in the first two seconds.
- Vary the angle across the set. Do not give me ten versions of the same idea.
- Make it work on mute: readable on-screen text, no reliance on audio.
- Vertical, 9:16.

When they are generated, use the Meta Ads MCP to publish them into a NEW
campaign, and create it PAUSED so nothing starts spending. Put each variation
in its own ad set so I can read the results per creative, name everything
clearly, and then give me a summary of what you built and what each variation
is testing.

Do not turn the campaign on. Leave it paused for me to review.

Step 5: Keep it from spending money you did not agree to

This is the step that protects you, so read it before you run anything.

Claude has write access to your ad account. That means it can create campaigns, and a campaign that is not paused starts spending real money against whatever budget it was given. Always tell it to create things paused, then review every ad yourself in Ads Manager before you turn anything on.

Check the budget, the audience and the creative on each variation. Ten ads publishing themselves is only useful if you actually look at them first. Treat the generated set as a pile of candidates, not a finished campaign.

Step 6: Read the results per creative, not in aggregate

The reason the prompt puts each variation in its own ad set is so the numbers mean something. Ten ads in one ad set tells you the group did well. Ten ad sets tells you which hook did well, and that is the thing you reuse.

After a few days, hand it back to Claude and ask it to compare the variations against each other and against your old winners. Then feed what it finds into another round. That loop is the actual product here, not any single ad.

Play it straight

Ad platforms have rules and they enforce them on the creative, not on the tool that made it. Generated video is fine. Fabricated claims, invented testimonials, fake urgency and misleading before-and-afters are not, and they get accounts restricted rather than just ads rejected.

Run your own products or ones you genuinely have permission to run. Check every generated ad for claims you cannot support before you unpause anything, because your ad account is the asset and it is the thing you lose.

Frequently asked questions

There is a free unlimited window open on the MCP connector. Tap here to claim it . Once you redeem it a 24 hour countdown starts, so finish the setup in step 1 before you activate it.

No. Both connectors are a URL you paste into Claude's connector settings. The only things you type after that are the two prompts on this page.

It can create campaigns, which is why both the prompt and step 5 tell it to create everything paused . A paused campaign spends nothing. Review each ad in Ads Manager and turn things on yourself. Never leave that to the model.

Because that is the whole advantage. Anyone can generate ten ads. Generating ten aimed at the hooks that already work in your specific account is a different thing, and it only happens if Claude reads the data first.

So you learn which creative won rather than just that the batch did alright. Per-creative results are what you feed into the next round, and the compounding is in that loop.

Generated video is not against the rules. The claims inside it can be. Check every ad for anything you cannot substantiate before unpausing, and keep fabricated results and fake testimonials out entirely.
